# Advanced vector operations: Dot Product and Cross Product

Source: [1963](https://workshop.codes/wiki/articles/1963); edited 2023-08-01. Evidence: archived documentation.

Not independently verified in the current game. An article edit date is not a behavioral test date.

<a id="wiki-1963-n1"></a>

- For normalized direction D, Dot Product(V,D) is signed directional magnitude; projection is D*Dot(D,V), residual is V minus projection.

<a id="wiki-1963-n2"></a>

- Impulse using negative residual direction and its magnitude with Incorporate Contrary Motion removes off-axis momentum; scaling magnitude removes a fraction.

<a id="wiki-1963-n3"></a>

- Cross-product operand order changes the sign; parallel vectors yield zero magnitude.

<a id="wiki-1963-n4"></a>

- Build camera-relative right/up axes from normalized cross products, then position an entity at eye + facing*depth + right*x + up*y.

Source limitations:

- Screen-space construction has no explicit fallback when facing is parallel to world Up; cross products become zero.

- Projection identities require normalized D as stated; treating arbitrary direction magnitude as unit would change results.

- Cross-source contradiction: tutorial says Forward cross Right is Up, but archived axis constants give Forward=(0,0,1), Right=(-1,0,0), and its stated cross-product formula yields Down. Articles 4585/4686/4732/4758 support the axis convention; correct/retest the example.
